llm_proposer.assessment: The evidence localizes the degradation to optical channel och57 on the S05→S15→S04 route, most likely at the S05 ROADM output toward S15. The channel loses power and OSNR at S15, the impairment persists to S04, and aggregate amplifier telemetry is unchanged; the fact that only the SNCP services are degraded while services on matching working routes remain healthy indicates that the affected services are currently using a common protection resource carried by och57.

proposals.rationale: Channel-specific attenuation at the S05 ROADM toward S15 directly explains O2/O4 and the downstream OSNR and BER degradation O1/O3/O5, while aggregate amplifier powers can remain unchanged. The main limitation is that no outbound per-channel monitor at S05 is reported to confirm the loss begins there.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment

proposals.rationale: Gain tilt in an amplifier on S05→S15 could weaken och57 while leaving aggregate input/output power and pump-current measurements effectively unchanged. It is less likely than WSS attenuation because no other edge-band channels are reported affected and no amplifier telemetry changed.

Added loss immediately upstream of the S15 monitor would produce the observed channel power and OSNR reductions and their propagation to S04. It normally affects all channels and may alter adjacent amplifier input/output readings, neither of which is observed.
proposals.note: nothing at that location documents the mode

proposals.rationale: A contaminated OMS patch could add loss before the S15 observation point. This is unlikely because its documented effect is across all channels, whereas the evidence is concentrated on och57 and aggregate line telemetry is stable.

A shifted WSS passband could create channel-specific quality degradation that propagates to the S04 receiver. However, its documented signature has normal power, contrary to the pronounced channel-power drop in O2.
proposals.note: site named; resolved to its node equipment
